issues.description: Template repository's Farm.java declares a class named AnimalFarm instead of Farm. The problem statement and solution expect a class named Farm (see UML and solution), so students will be unable to locate or implement the intended Farm class and will face confusion and compile errors when following the instructions that reference Farm.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename or replace the template file so it declares public class Farm in package de.tum.cit.ase (matching the problem statement and solution). Provide a clean, compile-able stub: package declaration, public class Farm { private List<Animal> animals; public Farm() { /* initialize */ } /* stubs for addAnimal, feedAllAnimals, singFarmSong */ }. This will align template, problem description, and solution structure.

issues.description: The template Farm.java file is syntactically malformed: it contains nested/duplicate 'package' declarations and a duplicated class body inside methods (unexpected package declaration and class text inside singFarmSong), which will cause compilation errors and prevent students from implementing the exercise. This is an unintentional structural corruption rather than an intentional pedagogical gap.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the nested/duplicated package declaration and duplicate class content from Farm.java. Replace the file with a correct, minimal stub that compiles (single package declaration at top, one public class Farm, method stubs and correct imports). Use the solution's Farm.java as a reference for correct structure and placement of methods and helper functions.

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution expect a class named 'Farm' (the UML and solution implement a public class Farm), but the template repository's Farm.java declares a public class named 'AnimalFarm'. This mismatch between the expected class identifier ('Farm') and the template's class identifier ('AnimalFarm') breaks the direct mapping from the exercise description to the starter code and will confuse students when they try to implement or use the Farm class (e.g., tests or the Main class expect 'Farm').
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class in the template from 'AnimalFarm' to 'Farm' (i.e., change 'public class AnimalFarm' to 'public class Farm') so the public class name matches the file name Farm.java and aligns with the problem statement and solution. Ensure any references in the template to 'AnimalFarm' are updated to 'Farm' and that the class provides the no-argument constructor and methods specified in the exercise.
